replacements.text: Strongest feature: Craig grants Flew’s conclusion under Aquinas, then identifies its theory-dependent premise by contrasting Thomistic premotion with Molina’s concurrence: God produces the effect alongside, rather than moving, the creaturely will, preserving alternatives. Principal limitation: This is a model-dependent escape, since middle knowledge, libertarian counterfactuals, and concurrence with unpremoved choice remain insufficiently justified, while divine responsibility for world-selection is unresolved. Live burden: Craig must substantiate modal commitments and reconcile world-selection with responsibility; Flew must challenge Molinism instead of assuming Thomistic concurrence uniquely governs omnipotent action. Locked score: The exact 83 reflects logical coherence 83, evidence warrant 73, responsiveness 90, relevance and burden 83, precision and clarity 85, and calibration and charity 85: direct, charitable engagement and differentiation outweigh underdefended metaphysics without eliminating that evidential deficit.

Strongest feature: Flew concedes morality yet denies Craig’s grounding conditional, invoking Hume’s common standards to distinguish wrongness from dislike and question whether objectivity requires divine command. Principal limitation: Common standards may explain agreement without establishing mind-independent authority; Flew neither shows why standards bind nor addresses error, while reducing Craig’s grounding thesis to command dependence narrows its claim. Live burden: Flew must provide a nondivine account of normative truth and obligation; Craig must show divine grounding supplies necessity and avoids arbitrariness. Locked score: The exact 76 reflects logical coherence 76, evidence warrant 65, responsiveness 83, relevance and burden 83, precision and clarity 77, and calibration and charity 76: decisive premise-contact and consistent independence are constrained by thin ontological warrant and partial conflation of grounding with command.
